IN  S.B. CRIMINAL REVISION PETITION NO.365/1995  (Satya Narain Vs. State of Rajasthan)
Date of Order : 02.08.2016  HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE GOVERDHAN BARDHAR Mr. J.K. Chanda, for the petitioner.
Mr. L.R. Upadhyay, Public Prosecutor.
BY THE COURT

entities.text: S.B. CRIMINAL REVISION PETITION NO.365/1995  (Satya Narain Vs. State of Rajasthan)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The petitioner by way of present revision petition under Section 397/401 Cr.P.C. has assailed the impugned judgment dated 31.10.1995 passed by learned Additional Sessions Judge No.3, Jodhpur (hereinafter "the Appellate Court") in Criminal Appeal No.10/1995 whereby the learned appellate Court has has upheld the judgment dated 02.08.1995, passed by the Chief Judicial Magistrate,
Jodhpur (for short "the trial court") in Cr. Case No.79/1989 whereby the trial court convicted the accused- petitioner for offence under Section 7/16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (for short, 'P.F.A. Act') and sentenced him to undergo one year's simple imprisonment alongwith fine of Rs. 2000/- and in default thereof to undergone three months' simple imprisonment.

Brief facts, giving rise to this revision petition are that on 19.07.1989, the complainant inspected the accused-petitioner's factory in the name and style of Namdev Ice Factory, Bilara and took samples of Ice Candy.
Upon sending the sample to the Public Analyst, it was found to be misbranded.

Accordingly, upon obtaining sanction from the competent authority, the case S.B. CRIMINAL REVISION PETITION NO.365/1995 (Satya Narain Vs. State of Rajasthan) was registered against the accused-petitioner.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Before framing of charge, statement of Jagdish (PW-1) was recorded.
The learned trial Court framed charge against the petitioner for offence punishable under Section 7/16 of P.F.A Act.
The accused- petitioner denied the charge and claimed for trial.
After conclusion of the prosecution evidence, statement of the accused-petitioner under Section 313 Cr.P.C. was recorded.

The learned trial Court, thereafter, heard final arguments and by its judgment dated 02.08.1995 convicted the accused- petitioner for offence under Section 7/16 of the Act and passed the sentence of one year's simple imprisonment with fine of Rs.2000/-.
In default of payment of fine, the trial court ordered that accused-petitioner shall undergo three months' simple imprisonment.
Being aggrieved by the judgment of the learned trial Court, the accused-petitioner approached the learned appellate Court.
The appellate Court by its judgment dated 31.10.1995 dismissed the petitioner's appeal and upheld the conviction and sentence awarded by the trial court.

sentences.text: 1 At the outset, learned counsel for the petitioner submits that he is not challenging the conviction of the petitioner for offence under Section 7/16 of the Act recorded by the learned trial court and affirmed by the learned appellate court but his only prayer is for issuance of direction to the State Government to consider case of the petitioner for commutation of sentence.

Learned counsel for the petitioner further submits that the petitioner is not a habitual offender and therefore, his case for commutation of sentence can very well be considered by the S.B. CRIMINAL REVISION PETITION NO.365/1995 (Satya Narain Vs. State of Rajasthan) Government under Section 433(d) Cr.P.C.

sentences.text: Learned Public Prosecutor has not opposed the prayer in general and submitted that in some of the identical cases, directions have been issued by the Court for consideration of commutation of sentence.
I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the materials available on record.
It is not disputed that the petitioner is not a habitual offender and therefore, the prayer to examine the case of the petitioner for commutation of sentence is acceptable.

In N.Sukumaran (supra), Supreme Court examined the matter pertaining to offence under Section 7/16 of the Act on the touchstone of Section 433(d) Cr.P.C. and held :
"3. The offence took place in the year 1984.
The appellant has been awarded six months' simple imprisonment and has also been ordered to pay a fine of Rs.1,000.00
Under clause (d) of Section 433 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, "the appropriate government" is empowered to commute the sentence of simple imprisonment for fine.
We think that this would be an appropriate case for commutation of sentence where almost a decade has gone by.

We, therefore, direct the appellant to deposit in the trial court a sum of Rs.6,000.00 as fine in commutation of the sentence of six months' simple imprisonment within a 5 period of six weeks form today and intimate to the appropriate government that such fine has been deposited.

On deposit of such fine, the State Government may formalise S.B. CRIMINAL REVISION PETITION NO.365/1995 (Satya Narain Vs. State of Rajasthan) the matter by passing appropriate orders under clause (d) of Section 433 of the Code of Criminal Procedures."

sentences.text: A co-ordinate Bench of this Court in Deva(supra) following the verdict in N.Sukumaran (supra) and taking into account the fact that incident is too old, held as under :
"9. The offence took place in the year 1981.
The accused petitioner has been awarded the imprisonment as indicated above.
Under Clause (d) of Section 433 of the Cr.P.C.
The appropriate government is empowered to commute the sentence of simple imprisonment for fine.

10. I think that this would be an appropriate case for Satya Narayan vs State on 2 August, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/130419148/

sentences.text: I, therefore, direct the petitioner to deposit in the trial Court a sum of Rs.6,000/- as fine in commutation of the sentence of six months simple imprisonment within a period of six weeks from today and intimate to the appropriate government that such fine has been deposited.

On deposit of such fine, the State Government may formalise the matter by passing appropriate orders; under Clause (d) of Section 433 of Cr.P.C. Till then the petitioner will remain on same bail bonds."
Undisputedly, since conviction of the petitioner, there is nothing adverse against him so as to prove that he is involved in food adulteration.

In this view of the matter and considering the fact that incident has occurred about 26 years back, I deem it just and appropriate to direct the petitioner to deposit a sum of Rs.7,500/- as fine before learned trial Court in commutation of sentence of one year's simple imprisonment for offence under Section 7/16 of the Act within a period of two months from today.

After deposition of the aforesaid amount, the petitioner may intimate the appropriate Government so as to formalize the S.B. CRIMINAL REVISION PETITION NO.365/1995 (Satya Narain Vs. State of Rajasthan) matter by passing appropriate orders; under Clause (d) of Section 433 Cr.P.C.
